Wikivoyage guide for Trincomalee (all topics):
[Introduction] Trincomalee is a city in eastern Sri Lanka. Trinco (as it is often called) is emerging as a tourist destination thanks to its incredible history and beaches, especially those just north of town.
[Understand] Trincomalee, once known as Gokarna, has been a key center of Tamil culture for centuries. The Koneswaram Temple, dating back to at least the 7th century, is a major landmark. Thanks to its natural harbour, traders from Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and Asia have been stopping by for generations. Trincomalee is situated on the 5th largest natural deepwater harbour in the world, for which it was fought over as a strategic naval base. ...
[Get in] By plane: Cinnamon Air flies daily from Colombo (Bandaranaike International Airport). The duration of the flight is 45 minutes. Fares are US$150-200 depending on season. By bus: The bus station is across the street from the clock tower and the market. Buses to Kandy leave at 04:00, around 9:15, 10:15, 13:45 and 14:45. The bus at 09:15 is supposed to have A/C and needs to be pre-booked, all other buses are standard (non-A/C) public buses. ...
[Get around] Trincomalee itself is a very compact town, so you can get around on foot. For longer trips, for example to Uppuveli, rickshaws are available at nearly every corner. Negotiate your fare before boarding if there is no meter — a rule of thumb is around Rs 100 per km. For Nilaveli, tuktuk drivers will want a flat price per person. ...
[See] Pigeon Island. Sri Lanka's only marine national park has great beaches for swimming, sunbathing and snorkelling. Turtles and black-tip reef sharks can be seen but the majority of the island's coral reef has been killed as of 2025. 1 Fort Fredrick. Fort Fredrick is an old Dutch fort dating back to 1665 located on a peninsula North East of the town center. ...
[Do] 1 Kanniya Hot Wells. 07:00-19:00 daily. An unusual spring with seven hot wells, popular among locals who use the hot spring water in the various "wells" for bucket showers. The facilities are badly maintained though, so bring a large towel to change your clothes as the change rooms are very dirty. Do not wear only a swimsuit as this will cause offence. Your accommodation will probably be able to lend you a bucket to take. ...
[Sleep] Very few tourists stay in Trincomalee itself. When tourists visit Trinco, they tend to stay in Uppuveli, 5km north of town, for its beaches. 10km further north is the popular tourist town of Nilaveli, which Wikivoyage treats as a separate town. The two main regions where guesthouses can be found are along the beach at Uppuveli and beyond, and south of Fort Frederick on the beach. Shop around as prices vary greatly. ...

Wikivoyage guide for Trincomalee (see and do):
[See] Pigeon Island. Sri Lanka's only marine national park has great beaches for swimming, sunbathing and snorkelling. Turtles and black-tip reef sharks can be seen but the majority of the island's coral reef has been killed as of 2025. 1 Fort Fredrick. Fort Fredrick is an old Dutch fort dating back to 1665 located on a peninsula North East of the town center. It has a long and storied history and was the site of battles involving (at different times) the Portuguese, Dutch, French and English navies. It is still actively garrisoned, but is open to visitors and is a great place to explore, especially for history buffs. There is a nice Hindu temple atop the cliff at the end of the peninsula with spectacular views. There are also kiosks where you can relax with a cold coconut. Friendly spotted deer roam the fort's forested areas, apparently descendents of a pair kept as pets by an English family in the 1800s. US$10. (updated Aug 2025) 2 Commonwealth War Cemetery, Nilaveli Rd. The final resting place of over 600 Allied soldiers and sailors who died in Trincomalee during World War II. You will be asked for a donation upon entering. ...
[Do] 1 Kanniya Hot Wells. 07:00-19:00 daily. An unusual spring with seven hot wells, popular among locals who use the hot spring water in the various "wells" for bucket showers. The facilities are badly maintained though, so bring a large towel to change your clothes as the change rooms are very dirty. Do not wear only a swimsuit as this will cause offence. Your accommodation will probably be able to lend you a bucket to take. The bathing area is very small and it gets crowded especially on the weekends. Hundreds of stalls line the road at the entrance. Rs 500 for foreigners. (updated Jun 2025) 2 Snorkelling. A snorkelling trip to Pigeon Island is a must. There are local boats that will take you to this island for a fee of about US$30 (return). Snorkelling is a great way to see the abundant sea life. Sadly the coral is not respected by the locals. (updated Jun 2025) Dolphin and whale watching. There is dolphin and whale watching available from most of the guest houses on Uppaveli beach (high season only). (updated Jun 2025)
